purpose: Direct empirical test of the manuscript's stability-diversity trade-off theorem: report n_eff (diversity) AND flip rate p (stability) JOINTLY at each fingerprint granularity, never either alone.

MatterGen.description: Raw generator output (file 65498772) paired with CHGNet-relaxed output (file 65498775) via the corrected 'id'-column join (material_id in 65498775 is a re-sequenced 0..9999 counter, NOT the generation index; formula-match rate 100% under the 'id' join vs 0.01% under naive material_id join).
MatterGen.diversity_measured_on: CHGNet-relaxed (post-relaxation) fingerprints, consistent with generator_calibration convention

CrystalFormer.description: Raw generator output (file 65498616, n=999) paired with CHGNet-relaxed output (file 65498610, n=992) via material_id join; full population used (no subsampling, ~1000 total).
CrystalFormer.diversity_measured_on: CHGNet-relaxed (post-relaxation) fingerprints, consistent with generator_calibration convention

WyLLM-vanilla-DiffCSP++.description: Raw generator output only (file 65498649, n=1000). No paired CHGNet-relaxed/raw set exists for this generator in this corpus, so the STABILITY (flip-rate) half of this experiment is UNAVAILABLE for WyLLM-vanilla. Included in the DIVERSITY half only, because it is the most collision-prone released generator (generator_calibration: 649/999 distinct at standard settings, design effect 4.32) and therefore the population where coarsening is expected to cost diversity most.
WyLLM-vanilla-DiffCSP++.diversity_measured_on: Raw generator fingerprints (no relaxed counterpart available)

feasible_window_analysis.criterion: p <= 0.5 (majority of pairs keep the same fingerprint after relaxation) AND n_eff above the auditability frontier N* at gamma=0.5, m=8 (N*=10)

MatterGen.verdict: Feasible window EXISTS, but only at granularity level 1 (space group + orbits + composition, no cell shape). At level 1, p ranges 0.152-0.393 across the symprec sweep and n_eff stays at n=1500 (design effect ~1.0-1.01), far above N*=10. required_n at gamma=0.5,m=8 is small (20-45). Every level that adds cell-shape information (2 through 5) pushes p above 0.5 (up to 0.964 at level 5, symprec 0.01) with NO compensating diversity gain (n_eff stays pinned at n throughout) -- the window closes as soon as cell information is added, purely on the stability side.

CrystalFormer.verdict: Feasible window EXISTS, again only at granularity level 1: p ranges 0.016-0.047 (very low), n_eff stays at 958-991 (design effect ~1.008, essentially unchanged across ALL levels 1-5), required_n is 14 throughout. From level 2 onward p jumps to 0.50-0.72 with no diversity payoff -- same qualitative pattern as MatterGen: the window closes purely on the stability side, not because diversity needed to be traded away.

WyLLM-vanilla-DiffCSP++.note: Cannot state a feasible window directly (no paired relaxed set), but this is the generator where the trade-off's diversity side is real: n_eff rises monotonically from 179.6 (level 1, mean over the four symprec values; range 179.4-180.1) to 314.9 (level 5; range 314.5-315.9) as cell information is added, design effect falling from 6.6 to 4.2 -- i.e. dropping cell shape (level 1) that was diversity-free for MatterGen/CrystalFormer costs this repetitive generator roughly 43% of its already-thin effective diversity (179 vs 315). By the monotonic p-vs-level pattern seen in both paired generators, the symmetric prediction is that this generator's flip rate would ALSO rise with added cell granularity -- meaning WyLLM-vanilla is the one generator in this corpus for which the theorem's cost is plausibly paid on both sides at once, though this cannot be confirmed without a paired relaxed set.

theorem_test_verdict.statement: The stability-diversity trade-off theorem predicts that no single fingerprint refinement can buy diversity without paying stability. The direct joint test on the two generators with paired raw/relaxed structures (MatterGen, CrystalFormer) shows the trade-off manifests ASYMMETRICALLY at this population size: adding cell-shape information (levels 2-5) uniformly INCREASES the flip rate p (MatterGen: 0.15-0.39 -> 0.59-0.96; CrystalFormer: 0.02-0.05 -> 0.50-0.72) while NEVER increasing n_eff beyond its already-near-n ceiling (design effect stays within 1.000-1.009 for both generators at every level) -- i.e. for these two chemically-diverse, high-n_eff generators, the diversity side of the trade never binds because composition+orbit information alone already separates almost every structure; the coarsening cost is paid entirely in stability with zero diversity return. On the collision-prone WyLLM-vanilla-DiffCSP++ (diversity-only half), the same coarsening produces a real, substantial diversity cost (n_eff 179->315 across levels, design effect 6.6->4.2), consistent with the theorem's mechanism operating precisely where a generator's chemical/structural diversity is already thin. This is a negative result for the SPECIFIC claim that the trade-off always binds on both axes simultaneously for any generator, and a positive, mechanistically consistent result for the theorem's underlying claim once diversity is not already saturated.
theorem_test_verdict.feasible_window_location: Granularity level 1 (SG + orbits + composition, no cell shape) for both MatterGen and CrystalFormer, at any tested symprec in [0.01, 0.3].
theorem_test_verdict.caveat: The feasible window at level 1 is the COARSEST tested setting, i.e. the setting closest to the fingerprint's floor of information content. This is consistent with -- not contradictory to -- the trade-off theorem: it says the window sits at low granularity, and every increment away from that floor moves p upward without buying diversity back for these two generators. Whether an even coarser fingerprint (dropping composition or orbit information) would eventually cost diversity was out of scope for this ablation (the granularity levels specified for fingerprint_ablation only vary cell-shape binning).
